questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Please explain: *
Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: For my study destination it was important for me that the destination had a rich culture, good weather and a good social life. It was also important for me to be in Europe because of the Erasmus grant but also because i would have a short way home for fx christmas. And i wanted to learn more about Europe.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Accommodation was great and really nice people. And the city was just so much nicer than expected.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. The faculty administration was very good and helpful. Also had a good communication with my home university, when i wanted to change one course. It was really nice to see that the two universities had good communication. It made it more safe for me.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received assistance with my courses, how to get the university card and the metro card for the city. I would have liked to get some information about some social life on university or something about some sport activities.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: I think it was easy. Social media makes it easy. My recommendations for future erasmus students is to sign up for as many groups on social media as you can. Also a good idea to write to the university and ask if they have any recommendations for specific websites.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: They should know that it is nice if you are more interested in the city than in the university. But they should also know that they will spend a lot of time on transportation since the campus is often outside the city center.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very few options, and those were either very expensive or in a very bad condition.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Good information in the first days with meetings and time to meet new students. This proces kept on going for 2-3 weeks so there was a lot of time to settle in and be sure that you knew everything you should. For future development they could maybe extend the deadline for when you should have chosen the courses you wanted. Give a week more for the students to get a better feeling about changing the courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: They had a good administration online with one very good coordinater. I felt that it was enough and i didnt have to wait for too long. Good response time online on email and also good response time when meeting up in person. I guess they also had help with the IT-services but it wasn't necessary for me or my fellow students.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Very succesfull. There was enough spots for all the courses i wanted, and i even wanted to change one, which i also was allowed to do.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: My best advice is that they should start in good time. Start the registration before exploring the city. This will ease the process and make it less stressfull so that the time in the city will be more efficient and nice. Its also a good idea to just ask as much as you can. When arriving in a place for the first time its totally fair to ask "dumb" questions.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I had 5 courses in total. I would say that the level was good, and i learned a lot when being on exchange. They were a bit easier than at my home university because there was less math than i was used to. But this was a good thing since there were a lot of other things to get to know and a whole new way of teaching.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Smaller crowds, which made it more productive i would say. They had time for all the questions. Compared to my home university Porto had no exercise classes, which could have helped in some of the courses.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Corporate finance, international trade, economic and public finance, organizational behaviour and economic growth.

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your second semester. *
What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Economic and public finance. good structure and useful stuff. I would also recommend international trade and coorperate finance, since they were very interesting and i learned a lot. Good teachers.

Local transportation DKK per month *
Food DKK per month *
Personal spending DKK per month *
Communication (phone, internet, etc.) DKK per month *

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I just did a lot more trips than i expected but i dont know if that is unexpected costs.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Shampoo were more expensive. Food in general were less expensive than expected. And also the beers and drinks when going out to party.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: I didn't see or hear so much. That is also what i wrote earlier that i wished for better activities there. especially with sports because that could help me with meeting locals and also just other international students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: For my university i really can't recommend any since i didn't participate in any.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I did an amazing trip to Madeira. Very beautiful and memories for life. I also did the camino from Porto to Santiago which is also something i will remember for the rest of my life. I can also recommend trips to the capital of Portugal, Lisbon. It's very cheap with bus and they arrive all the time, which makes it very easy.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was a bit tough since i didn't speak their language and their level of english was challenged. Apart from that they were very sweet and they wanted to greet me and make me feel welcome.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I can only recommend learning their language but also just approach them. Even though the maybe seem to be not interested its sometimes not the case. They are just shy sometimes.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: I found the tempo a bit challenging in the start because it was a lot slower than i am used to. But after a while i really started to like how they walked slow and just took everything in a slow tempo. I actually also found their food a bit challenging since it was not as good as i expected. Only meat options as well.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: As i mentioned above i learned to appreciate their tempo.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: The three most beautiful things is the amazing city of Porto. Then it is the social life and all the good international classes on the university.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: No, not other than they expect you to be fluent in english and that the exams is written on paper by hand.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The most rewarding part of my exchange was the self-realisation i had. I got to know myself a lot better in many ways, and also just got to know a new city into its core.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The greatest challenge was to be away from family and friends back home. I really missed them and the social life in Porto wasn't as good as back home. But that is also the reason why i got to know myself a lot more.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
